MeteoGalicia daily observations as a base R data.frame

Source: R/meteogal2df.R
meteogal2df.Rd

Download daily observations from MeteoGalicia, or read previously downloaded files, returning a plain data.frame (no sf geometry, no units classes). Every measurement keeps its MeteoGalicia validation code in a qc_<variable> column.

Usage

meteogal2df(
  station_ids = NULL,
  start_date = NULL,
  end_date = NULL,
  last_n_days = 30L,
  vars = NULL,
  file = NULL,
  data_dir = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  control = list(),
  quality = c(1L, 5L)
)

Arguments

station_ids

NULL for all stations or a character vector of IDs.

start_date, end_date

Optional Date or "YYYY-MM-DD". Online, the default is the last last_n_days days. With data_dir, NULL means unbounded.

last_n_days

Number of days used if no start_date is given online.

vars

NULL to keep all measurements, or a character vector of variable names (e.g. c("temp_mean", "prec")) or native parameter codes (e.g. "TA_AVG_1.5m"). Online, they are requested with idParam. The station/date fields and the matching qc_ columns are always kept.

file

Optional output file (.rds, .rda/.RData or .csv). The saved file contains the unfiltered values and codes; quality only affects the returned data.frame.

data_dir

NULL for online data, or a local directory or a single .rds/.rda/.csv file.

verbose

Show progress messages.

control

List with max_attempts (3), retry_wait (15 seconds), sleep_pause (1 second), window_days (NULL = calendar months) and timeout (60 seconds).

quality

Validation codes whose values are used (default c(1, 5)); any of 0, 1, 2, 5. NULL uses all values except codes 3 and 9.

Value

A data.frame with fecha (Date), station_id (character), station metadata (station_name, municipality, province, altitude, lon, lat when available), timestamp, the measurements and their qc_ columns. Attributes: quality (codes used) and units.

Details

Online requests use the documented daily JSON service (datosDiariosEstacionsMeteo.action) in calendar-month windows. For each measurement the service returns the value (valor), its validation code (lnCodigoValidacion) and its unit (unidade); the value goes to <variable>, the code to qc_<variable> and the units to attr(x, "units"). Values are never converted or imputed.

Validation codes (see meteogal_qc_codes()): 0 not validated, 1 valid original, 2 suspect, 3 erroneous, 5 valid interpolated, 9 not recorded. quality lists the codes whose values are returned; the rest are set to NA and a message reports how many values were affected and with which code. The codes always remain in the qc_ columns, so the decision can be inspected or changed later. The default quality = c(1, 5) keeps validated values only: recent data, not yet validated by MeteoGalicia (code 0), will therefore be NA unless quality = c(0, 1, 5) (or NULL) is used. Codes 3 and 9 and the value -9999 are always NA. For comparison, 'meteospain' (0.3.1) removes values with codes 0, 3 and 9 and discards the codes (it keeps suspect values, code 2).

Missing data: a day absent from the service response is absent from the returned data.frame (no row is invented); a value that is NA, -9999, or has code 3 or 9 is NA. February 29 is kept here; it is only removed in the functional representation.

Local files (data_dir): station-year files written by meteogal2download() (.rds or .csv, with codes), files saved with meteogal2df(file = ...), or any .csv/.rds/.rda data.frame with fecha, station_id and the variables. Data without qc_ columns are accepted: their validation status is unknown and their values are not modified (except -9999). With data_dir and no dates, everything available is read; online, the default is the last last_n_days days.

References

MeteoGalicia, daily JSON service (parameters, structure and validation codes): https://www.meteogalicia.gal/datosred/infoweb/meteo/docs/rss/JSON_EstacionsDiarios_es.pdf.

MeteoGalicia, historical data through the web form (manual query of the same network, not used by this package): https://www.meteogalicia.gal/datosred/infoweb/meteo/docs/informes/datos_es.pdf.

Legal notice (attribution required): https://www.meteogalicia.gal/aviso-legal.

See also

meteogal2download(), meteogal2inventory(), meteogal_qc_codes()

Examples

f <- system.file("extdata", "meteogal_small.csv", package = "meteogal2fdata")
x <- meteogal2df(data_dir = f, vars = c("temp_mean", "prec"))
head(x)
#>        fecha station_id             station_name province altitude       lon
#> 1 2024-01-01      10157 Coruña-Torre de Hércules A Coruña       21 -8.409202
#> 2 2024-01-02      10157 Coruña-Torre de Hércules A Coruña       21 -8.409202
#> 3 2024-01-03      10157 Coruña-Torre de Hércules A Coruña       21 -8.409202
#> 4 2024-01-04      10157 Coruña-Torre de Hércules A Coruña       21 -8.409202
#> 5 2024-01-05      10157 Coruña-Torre de Hércules A Coruña       21 -8.409202
#> 6 2024-01-06      10157 Coruña-Torre de Hércules A Coruña       21 -8.409202
#>        lat temp_mean prec
#> 1 43.38276     12.59  0.0
#> 2 43.38276     15.10 10.6
#> 3 43.38276     14.04  0.0
#> 4 43.38276     12.52 16.4
#> 5 43.38276     11.49  4.1
#> 6 43.38276      9.90  0.5
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Online: last 30 days, also using values not yet validated (code 0)
x <- meteogal2df(station_ids = "10157", vars = c("temp_mean", "prec"),
                 quality = c(0, 1, 5))
table(x$qc_temp_mean, useNA = "ifany")
} # }
